newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: German economy "not bad" in April, May - Issing.
newsitem.headline: German economy "not bad" in April, May - Issing.

text.p: The German economy's performance was "not bad" in April and May, but special factors made comparisons difficult, Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing said.
First-quarter gross domestic product growth came in slightly better than expected at 0.5 percent versus the previous quarter, Issing told Swiss bankers in Zurich.

"The data we have seen since then confirm this impression. Based on the information we have, April and May were not so bad," he said, but the fact that Easter fell in March this year and May had so many holidays made the data hard to gauge.

"I mention this not because it is so important, but because order inflow data for May and production numbers have just been published. They do not appear intoxicating, but they have to be seen against this background," he said.
German industrial orders fell 0.8 percent in May compared with April, breaking a four-month uptrend. Industrial output edged down 0.2 percent in May from April, its first fall since January.
